---
engine: markdown
title: "Nanoplots"
subtitle: "In-cell plots, drawn natively and scaled against one domain."
description: "format-nanoplot and the three renderers Keisen ships: nanoplot-line, nanoplot-points, and nanoplot-bar."
---

A nanoplot cell holds any value the renderer's `readings` function can read numbers from, and [`format-nanoplot`](formatters.qmd) draws it through the renderer given as `plot`.
The domain spans every reading in the column, taken from the column itself, so the cells can be compared; that is the whole point, since sparklines scaled per cell say nothing.
`domain: (low, high)` overrides it for a column read against a scale that is not its own.

A nanoplot column sizes itself to the plot's `width` plus the cell inset on both sides, and a set `table-width` does not stretch it.
The plot's `width` is a length in `em` or `pt`, not a percentage.
A table with a nanoplot column needs `cell-inset` as a length or a dictionary of lengths, because the column width is computed from it.
Where [`columns-width`](columns.qmd) names the column, it must be a fixed length in `em` or `pt`, wider than twice the cell inset: the plot gets what the inset leaves.

Three renderers ship, each drawn with native Typst primitives and each built by calling it, as in `plot: nanoplot-line()`.

| Function | Notable arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `nanoplot-line(..)` | `stroke: auto`, `thickness: 0.6pt`. A sparkline. |
| `nanoplot-points(..)` | The same, plus `radius: 1pt`. A sparkline with its readings marked. |
| `nanoplot-bar(..)` | `fill: auto`, `gap: 30%`. Bars, measured from zero. |

: Nanoplot renderers {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

`stroke: auto` and `fill: auto` follow the surrounding text colour, so a plot in a styled cell is drawn in that cell's ink.
Bars are measured from zero rather than from the domain's low, because a bar drawn from 5 to 10 makes a small difference look like the whole quantity; the line renderers scale to the domain instead, since a trend is about shape rather than magnitude.

A renderer is a dictionary with the keys `kind`, `draw`, `readings` and `axis`, so one written in a document works exactly as well as these.

- `kind` is `"nanoplot-renderer"`.
- `draw(value, domain: .., width: .., height: ..)` returns the content for one cell.
- `readings(value)` returns the numbers in a cell value, and the column's domain is taken across them.
  It receives every cell value, `none` included, and must return `()` for a value it cannot read.
- `axis` is `none` in the shipped line, points and bar renderers; see [Axis](#axis) for a renderer that draws one.

A renderer can read records rather than plain numbers, because the cell value reaches `draw` as it is.
The shipped `draw` reads numbers only, so `draw` and `readings` must read the value the same way.
A renderer that changes `readings` alone draws a blank plot.

Both calls below format the same column of records.

The shipped renderer finds no numbers in a record, so the cell is blank:

```typst
#format-nanoplot("pay", plot: nanoplot-line())
```

A renderer that reads the salary draws it:

```typst
#let salaries(value) = if type(value) == array { value.map(record => float(record.salary)) } else { () }
#let by-salary = nanoplot-line() + (
  readings: salaries,
  draw: (records, domain: none, width: 4em, height: 0.8em) => (nanoplot-line().draw)(
    salaries(records), domain: domain, width: width, height: height,
  ),
)
#format-nanoplot("pay", plot: by-salary)
```

## Axis

The `axis` key of a renderer is `none`, or a function that draws an axis.
`axis(domain: .., width: .., side: ..)` takes named arguments only, where `side` is `"top"` or `"bottom"`, and it returns content or `none`.
The domain is the one the column's plots share, and the width is the width of the plot inside the cell.

A renderer with an axis adds up to two rows to the table.
The top row sits at the end of the repeating column header, right after the column labels.
The bottom row sits right after the last body row, before any summary rows that follow it.
Columns whose renderer draws no axis on that side get an empty cell in the row.
A column with no readings has no domain and gets no axis.

The axis rows are not body rows.
Striping, summaries, `rows` selectors, locations and styles do not see them.

The table below draws an axis that writes the domain of the `trend` column.
The `plain` column beside it has no axis.

```{typst}
//| file: ../../tests/visual/nanoplots-axis.typ

The trend column has a small axis label reading 0.9 to 2.1 under its column label, and the same label again under the last body row, above the final Total row. Each body row holds a sparkline in the trend column and another in the plain column, which has no axis label."
```
